idea.description: SASRec predicts the next item by using causal self-attention to select relevant interactions from a user's history. It combines item and position embeddings, attention blocks and feed-forward layers, then scores candidates against the resulting sequence representation. It can emphasize recent actions or longer dependencies. Source: [Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation](https://arxiv.org/html/1808.09781).
idea.motivation: Sparse histories favor simple transition patterns, while richer histories support longer dependencies. SASRec learns which historical items matter. However, standard SASRec requires interaction history and learned item embeddings; it does not itself solve zero-interaction user or item cold start.
idea.implementation_notes: Start from RecHarness sasrec_perdataset and preserve routing for all four categories. Use preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42 and the environment default SASREC_EPOCHS=200. Keep DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'] and artifacts beneath the trial directory. Select configurations using the pinned macro-average validation HR@10 only, within 43,200 shared GPU-seconds. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), measured metrics with definitions, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Any architecture change must update both compatibility probes and the predictor writer. No benchmark results or concrete cold-start extension were supplied.
idea.pseudocode:
For each category:
  Load the unchanged benchmark split.
  Build padded training histories and shifted next-item targets.
  Encode item and position embeddings using causal attention.
  Score positive and sampled negative items; optimize masked binary cross-entropy.
  Save model configuration, weights and dataset routing beneath the trial directory.
Run the pinned validation procedure and select by mean category HR@10.
Generate working/predict.py with the matching architecture and routing.

originality.positive: The original paper introduced an effective self-attention approach to sequential recommendation.
originality.negative: The supplied idea reuses the existing SASRec baseline and specifies no novel cold-start mechanism. Scores use a 1–10 scale.

future_potential.positive: Available titles and descriptions could support a future content-based extension for items with few interactions.
future_potential.negative: This extension is a proposal, not part of the supplied method; improvement requires measured validation.

code_difficulty.positive: The existing per-dataset SASRec baseline provides the main training and inference structure.
code_difficulty.negative: Architecture changes require coordinated checkpoint loading, predictor generation and diagnostic compatibility. Higher scores indicate greater difficulty.

report:
Matched RecHarness Amazon task: four datasets Movies_and_TV,
Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl, macro-average validation
HR@10. Start from RecHarness sasrec_perdataset. Preprocessing seed=0 and training
seed=42, exactly as run2.sh. The host executes your train.py and then independently
evaluates working/predict.py using the pinned RecHarness benchmark (200 validation
users/category, 99 unique negative candidates, evaluation seed=42). Test labels and
test metrics are unavailable during search. Retain all four categories and dataset
routing. DATA_DIR must remain os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write artifacts beneath
your trial directory, as the baseline does. Training may change model architecture,
loss, optimizer, sampling and hyperparameters, as in RecHarness. Do not alter input
splits, invent metrics, read hidden test files, fetch extra datasets/pretrained weights,
or change the host evaluator. Changes to inference must also update the predictor
writer so working/predict.py loads the trained architecture. Keep execution single-GPU;
the host provides four concurrent trial slots and 64 CPU cores. No shell actions,
filesystem inspection, or training tools are needed in the LLM call: return code.
All training, diagnostics, debugging and failed trials consume the method's shared
43,200 GPU-second search budget. LLM time and final held-out inference are recorded
separately, matching run2.sh's separate final-evaluation step.
The original RecHarness tools layer sets SASREC_EPOCHS=200 (overriding the template's
standalone default of 300); this same environment default applies here.
